name: Arabians
overview: The Bible records the Arabians as a significant people interacting with Israel and Judah in various ways. They were involved in military actions against Judah, as seen when the LORD stirred up the Arabians alongside other nations to invade Judah during Jehoram's reign, resulting in the capture of his family (2 Chronicles 21:16-17). They also opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls during Nehemiah's time, mocking and resisting the efforts of God's people (Nehemiah 2:19; 4:7). Additionally, prophetic passages highlight the Arabians as inhabitants of the desert regions, providing sustenance and refuge, indicating their role in commerce and travel (Isaiah 21:13-14). These references reflect a complex relationship marked by conflict, opposition, and interaction with God's covenant people.
